We recorded dorsal CA1 neurons in five rats navigating a route that included two motor-driven treadmills, with the treadmill delay changed blockwise. About half of the pyramidal neurons (45 of 89, in four of five animals) showed temporally modulated firing that improved cross-validated prediction of spiking beyond measured position and head movement. Most of these neurons (36 of 45) fired transiently at treadmill onset, after treadmill offset, or both, and their transition-related firing profiles were neuron-specific and recurred across task stages. When the delay was doubled, post-offset responses shifted with treadmill offset rather than remaining at a fixed time from onset; this effect was consistent within the recorded animals but was not established across animals. Post-offset responses coincided with the resumption of movement. These findings indicate that CA1 temporal modulation is not confined to activity within the delay but is also aligned to the end of the delay, when navigation resumes, and suggest that transition-related CA1 activity may help link successive phases of structured behavior.

title: Genetically selected alcohol-preferring rats show increased heroin self-administration and upregulated VTA Oprm1 expression.
abstract: Alcohol use disorder and opioid use disorder (OUD) are chronic relapsing conditions that share genetic and neurobiological substrates, particularly within mesolimbic circuits and opioid receptor signaling. Understanding their overlapping genetic vulnerabilities is crucial for developing translational models of cross-vulnerability. The Marchigian Sardinian alcohol-preferring (msP) rat line, selectively bred for high alcohol intake and preference, displays altered expression of stress- and opioid-related genes, including Oprm1, which encodes the μ-opioid receptor (MOP). However, Oprm1 expression and function in the ventral tegmental area (VTA), a key region mediating drug reinforcement, had not yet been characterized in this strain. Quantitative PCR revealed higher Oprm1 mRNA levels in the VTA of male msP rats compared to Wistars, while no difference was observed in females. Across two independent cohorts, male msP rats self-administered significantly more heroin than Wistar controls. To test causality between higher VTA Oprm1 expression and higher heroin self-administration, Oprm1 expression was downregulated in the VTA via shRNA, resulting in reduction of heroin self-administration over time with a larger effect in msP than Wistar rats. These findings indicate that elevated VTA Oprm1 expression contributes to the higher heroin self-administration observed in male msP rats. Given the lack of selectively bred lines for opioid preference, the msP strain offers a valuable genetic model for studying vulnerability to OUD and for exploring mechanisms underlying alcohol-opioid cross-vulnerability.

title: A high-precision whole-brain 3D atlas of GABAergic neurons: sex difference analysis based on fMOST/SHIELD and association with neuropsychiatric disorders.
abstract: γ-Aminobutyric acid (GABA) ergic neurons play a critical role in regulating neural circuit activity and are implicated in various neuropsychiatric disorders, including autism spectrum disorder. However, a comprehensive whole-brain 3D atlas of GABAergic neurons with high precision and its association with sex differences and neuropsychiatric disorders has been lacking. In this study, we utilized fluorescence micro-optical sectioning tomography (fMOST) combined with stabilization of hydrogels for imaging and elimination of dyes (SHIELD) tissue clearing technology to generate a high-precision whole-brain 3D atlas of GABAergic neurons at submicron resolution using glutamic acid decarboxylase 67-green fluorescent protein (GAD67-GFP) knock-in mice. We found that the number of GAD67-positive cells in the male mice's main olfactory bulb (MOB), caudate nucleus (CP), hemispheric area (HEM), ventral area (VERM), and motor-related superior colliculus (SCm) was significantly higher than that in female mice, whereas the number of GAD67-positive cells in the female mice's somatosensory cortex (SS) was significantly higher than that in males; no gender differences were observed in other brain regions. Validation experiments combining fMOST data with immunofluorescence (IF) staining confirmed the specificity of GAD67-GFP labeling for GABAergic neurons. Furthermore, cross-validation using the Allen Brain Atlas and MERFISH datasets confirmed the reliability of our GABAergic neuron mapping. Our findings provide a valuable resource for understanding sex differences in GABAergic neuron distribution, as well as the relationship between GABAergic neuron density and neuropsychiatric disorders.

title: Vascular-targeted mild photothermal modulation of the blood-brain barrier enables efficient delivery of Pt(IV) prodrug to glioblastoma.
journal: Journal of controlled release : official journal of the Controlled Release Society
abstract: Effective platinum chemotherapy for glioblastoma is constrained by the blood-brain barrier and blood-brain tumor barrier (BBB/BBTB), which limit intracranial drug exposure. Here, we developed PS@RGD-Pt nanoparticles that integrate a NIR photothermal semiconducting polymer, a reduction-responsive Pt(IV)-backbone polymer, and cRGD-functionalized PEG-PLGA to couple vascular targeting, mild photothermal barrier modulation, and intracellular platinum activation. In orthotopic GL261 gliomas, cRGD promoted nanoparticle localization at tumor-associated vessels. Irradiation by an 808 nm laser at 0.5 W/cm2 for 3 min raised the tumor-site temperature to 46.3 °C and transiently reorganized Claudin-5 and ZO-1. Extending irradiation to 6 min raised the temperature to 63 °C and induced glial activation, delineating a thermal-dose window. BBB/BBTB permeability peaked at 1 h and approached baseline within 24 h, without detectable alterations in vascular density, cerebral perfusion, neuronal or glial markers, memory, or locomotion. Within this mild photothermal window, intratumoral platinum accumulation increased by approximately 4.6-fold with low accumulation in the contralateral normal brain. Reduction-responsive activation of Pt(IV) enhanced tumor DNA damage and apoptosis. PS@RGD-Pt with irradiation prolonged median survival to 36 days, compared with 16 days for PBS, 20 days for nonirradiated PS@RGD-Pt, and 22 days for RGD-Pt with irradiation, while reducing systemic toxicity relative to cisplatin. These findings establish vascular-targeted, mild photothermal BBB modulation as a controllable strategy that couples reversible barrier opening with tumor-responsive platinum activation for glioblastoma treatment.

title: Chirped speech (Cheech) enables rapid assessment of multi-level auditory evoked potentials during speech-in-noise recognition.
abstract: Difficulties understanding speech in noise remain a common complaint even among listeners with normal hearing sensitivity, highlighting the need for objective, more effective measures of real-world listening. The goal of this study was to validate the use of a novel, chirped-speech (Cheech) stimulus-continuous, naturally-spoken speech fused with chirps designed to elicit robust auditory evoked potentials-to characterize relationships between speech recognition, listening effort, and auditory neural encoding. Twenty‑five normal‑hearing adults completed a sentence‑recognition task using both original (unmodified) and Cheech-modified AzBio sentence lists in quiet, +3 dB, and -3 dB signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) conditions while neural responses from the brainstem through cortex were recorded simultaneously. Speech recognition remained near ceiling in quiet but declined with decreasing SNR for both original and Cheech stimuli. Cheech‑modified speech showed poorer recognition performance as SNR decreased and somewhat higher perceived effort overall. Yet, Cheech was highly effective at evoking auditory responses from the brainstem (auditory brainstem response, ABR) through the cortex (including middle- and late-latency responses, MLR and LLR) even with <5 min listening time per condition. Neural responses showed reduced amplitudes and prolonged latencies as SNR decreased. In general, ABR wave I latencies were associated with speech-in-noise recognition performance, whereas cortical responses (MLR Na and LLR P1 latencies) were associated with subjective workload. These findings show that Cheech‑modified speech remains intelligible, particularly in quiet and higher SNR conditions, while yielding robust, multilevel neural recordings during sentence perception, offering a promising approach to examine hierarchical auditory processing under ecologically relevant speech‑in‑noise conditions.

title: Social relevance reshapes memory encoding and promotes false memories across sensory modalities.
abstract: Memory is shaped not only by the information itself but also by its social relevance. The present study investigated whether, in the absence of misleading information, social relevance can increase false memory by altering encoding processes, and whether this effect depends on sensory modality. Using a social DRM paradigm combined with fNIRS, we manipulated item relevance (self-relevant, partner-relevant, irrelevant) and encoding modality (visual, auditory). Behavioral results showed that partner-relevant (vs. irrelevant) items elicited more false memories, indicating that social relevance can enhance false memory even in the absence of explicit misinformation. Neural findings revealed that socially relevant encoding elicited activity within frontal, temporal, and temporoparietal regions, consistent with the notion that social relevance may be linked to spontaneous monitoring processes. Further analyses indicated that frontal and temporal activity predicted subsequent false memory, whereas temporoparietal activity reflected social orienting rather than directly predicting memory distortion. These results suggest that false memory may arise not only from external misinformation but also from encoding biases triggered by social cues. Overall, this study provides new evidence for understanding how social contexts influence false memory and suggests that social relevance may shape subsequent memory performance through attentional and encoding-related processes.

title: Reproducible transversal mouse brain sections using low-cost 3D printable resin matrix.
abstract: Rodent brain matrices that produce coronal or sagittal brain sections for histology confer reproducibility and enable high throughput processing of tissues. However, a stainless steel or acrylic brain matrix that produces tissue sections in a transversal (or horizontal) orientation is currently unavailable as a standard tool. This limits the direct comparison of bilateral brain hemispheres within a single histological section, as freehand trimming to obtain horizontal planes is not easily replicable across samples. To mitigate this challenge, we designed a low-cost (USD 7 per unit), 3D-printed resin-based transverse brain matrix that accommodates mouse brains ranging from 12 to 16 mm in length from the olfactory bulb to the brainstem. Our matrix reproducibly generates horizontal tissue sections with a minimum of 1-mm-thickness without causing visible tissue deformation, which is comparable to the performance of commercial rodent brain matrices. We validated the quality of the horizontal brain tissue slices by histology and immunohistochemistry. Users may adapt the accompanying CAD code using our video tutorials to customize the transverse brain matrix for their specific needs, including alternative brain size, shape, and tissue thickness.

title: Epilepsy landscape in the Democratic Republic of Congo: A narrative review.
abstract: Epilepsy is a major public health problem in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), disproportionately affecting a young population in a context of limited resources. In this narrative review, we synthesise available epilepsy data from the DRC published between 1990 and 2025. No nationwide, population-based study has been conducted, and existing data come from heterogeneous sources, mostly hospital-based or small regional surveys. The overall epilepsy prevalence is estimated to be between 0.7 % and 1.8 % nationally, representing approximately 700,000 to 1,900,000 people living with epilepsy in a population of 105-109 million. The predominant epilepsy risk factors for epilepsy in DRC include perinatal encephalopathies, central nervous system infections, particularly cerebral malaria, neurocysticercosis, onchocerciasis, meningitis, and traumatic brain injuries. Recent clinic-based data suggest that the average age of seizure onset is 13.1 years +/- 11.2 years, with a wide range spanning from 5 days, and male-to-female ratios ranging from 1.1 to 1.9. Convulsive seizures dominate the clinical picture in the available series. The therapeutic gap remains considerable, with an estimated 75-80 % of people with epilepsy lacking access to appropriate care, a situation exacerbated by persistent sociocultural stigma, a shortage of neurologists (10 per 109 million inhabitants), and the scarcity of diagnostic and monitoring facilities. These findings underscore the urgent need for national management strategies that integrate prevention of avoidable causes, decentralised diagnostic services, improved access to antiseizure medication, and sustained community awareness campaigns.

title: Purinergic receptor P2X7 in cancer, neurodegeneration, and immune-mediated inflammatory diseases: mechanistic insights and therapeutic potential.
abstract: The P2X7 receptor (P2X7R), a ligand-gated cation channel activated by extracellular ATP, has gained significant attention as a key regulator of inflammatory signaling and a promising therapeutic target across diverse pathologies. Though classically characterized as a non-selective cation channel, P2X7R regulates multiple downstream processes, including Ca²⁺ influx, K⁺ efflux, NLRP3 inflammasome activation, cytokine release, and immune cell responses, thereby orchestrating innate and adaptive immune functions. In chronic inflammatory and immune-mediated disorders, dysregulated P2X7R signaling has been associated with persistent inflammation, aberrant immune activation, and disruption of tissue homeostasis. Evidence from various studies implicates P2X7R in the pathogenesis and progression of several neurological disorders, chronic inflammatory conditions and diverse cancer types. Nevertheless, the functional contribution of P2X7R is highly context-dependent and varies with disease state, cellular expression pattern, receptor activation status, and experimental model. This review provides a comprehensive overview of current knowledge regarding the genetic architecture, structural and physiological characteristics, activation mechanisms, and downstream signaling pathways of P2X7R, with particular emphasis on its involvement in disease pathogenesis and its potential as a therapeutic target. Furthermore, we critically evaluate the current challenges that have limited successful clinical translation, and highlight future perspectives for the development of P2X7R-directed therapies.

title: Cognitive trajectories across the menopausal transition in women with multiple sclerosis: an exploratory longitudinal cohort study.
abstract: Women with multiple sclerosis (MS) may be disproportionately vulnerable to cognitive symptoms during menopause because cognitive impairment is common in MS and sex hormone fluctuations may influence cognition and MS disease activity. The impact of menopause on cognition in the MS population is unknown. Retrospective analysis of prospectively collected cognitive data from five Australian MS centers (2016-2026). Menopause status was determined through retrospective surveys (2018-2026). MSReactor cognitive assessments and Women's Health survey responses were linked with prospective clinical data from the MSBase registry. The primary analysis included 28 participants (336 assessments) and a secondary exploratory analysis included 50 participants (493 assessments). Linear mixed-effects models assessed changes in cognitive trajectories across visual attention, processing speed, and working memory using Simple Reaction Time (SIRT), Choice Reaction Time (CHRT), and One Back Test (OBK) tasks. Models examined changes in slope anchored at menopause (primary analysis) and age 50 (secondary analysis). In the primary analysis, no evidence of a change in cognitive trajectory at menopause was observed (slope change: SIRT: β=10, 95% CI -14,34; CHRT: β=17, 95% CI -25,60; OBK: β=30, 95% CI -17,77). In the secondary analysis, CHRT and OBK showed evidence of a change in slope at age 50, with worsening reaction times before age 50 and relative stabilization thereafter (slope change: CHRT: β=-22, 95% CI -42,-2.7; OBK: β=-28, 95% CI -55,-0.91). This exploratory study did not identify a change in cognitive trajectory associated with menopause. However, the small sample size and wide confidence intervals mean clinically relevant effects cannot be excluded.

title: The role of early school performance on subsequent alcohol and drug use disorders: A Swedish cohort study.
abstract: To examine whether lower academic performance in compulsory school (age 15-16) increases the risk of later alcohol use disorder (AUD) and drug use disorder (DUD), and to assess the extent to which shared familial factors account for these associations. This national cohort study included 2937,919 individuals born in Sweden between 1972 and 2002, residing in Sweden on 1 July of the year in which school grades were assessed (ages 15-16 years), followed until first diagnosis of AUD without comorbid DUD, DUD without comorbid AUD, death, or December 31, 2023. Academic performance was measured using 9th-grade grade point average and categorized into deciles. Cox proportional hazards models estimated hazard ratios (HRs), and sibling-comparison models were used to adjust for shared familial genetic and environmental factors FINDINGS: Lower academic performance was strongly associated with increased risk of both AUD and DUD, showing a clear dose-response pattern across the full grade distribution. Risks were consistently higher for DUD than for AUD, and the associations remained robust in sibling-comparison analyses, although somewhat attenuated. Lower academic performance in adolescence is a strong predictor of later AUD and DUD, with markedly higher risks for DUD. Neither birth year, sex, maternal and paternal psychiatric history, parental income, nor the highest parental education origin, nor shared familial factors fully explain the association.

title: Quantification of microbubble-induced streaming across ultrasound frequencies using particle image velocimetry.
abstract: Functional microbubbles are widely used in therapeutic ultrasound for drug delivery, blood-brain barrier opening, clot lysis, and other biomedical interventions. Their therapeutic effects arise largely from acoustic microstreaming, which generates localized shear stresses and enhances transport around oscillating bubbles. Despite the central role of microstreaming, its dependence on ultrasound excitation conditions is not well defined. Existing studies use diverse and often incomparable frequencies, pressures, and duty cycles, leaving a gap in systematic understanding of how these parameters govern the streaming velocity and shear fields produced by functional microbubbles under physiologically relevant conditions. In this study, we employ particle image velocimetry (PIV) in a popliteal-vein lab-on-chip model to directly quantify the microstreaming velocity and shear-rate fields generated by microbubbles across a wide range of ultrasound conditions including frequency, duty cycle, and acoustic pressure. Measurements at 150 kHz, 300 kHz, 500 kHz, and 1 MHz reveal a pronounced frequency dependence. Counterintuitively, the strongest microstreaming is observed at 150 kHz, with progressively weaker streaming at 300 and 500 kHz, and the weakest flows at 1 MHz. This trend contrasts with the common assumption that microbubble oscillations peak near their ∼ 1MHz resonance frequency. Duty cycle further modulated the response: 10 % duty cycle generated the weakest fields, whereas 100 % duty cycle produced maximal streaming. Pressure-scaling was strongly frequency-dependent. At 150 kHz, raising the driving pressure from 100 to 300 kPa increased the mean streaming velocity by up to fourfold, whereas at 1 MHz the same pressure increase produced essentially no change in velocity. These findings underscore that acoustic frequency plays a substantial role in intensity of microbubble-induced streaming, with low-frequency excitation in the 150-300 kHz range producing markedly more efficient streaming and associated shear. Operating within this low-frequency window identifies therapeutically relevant velocity and shear levels, but choice of pressure must balance streaming efficacy against the narrow pressure range over which cavitation can be maintained at sub-MHz frequencies.

title: Knowledge, attitudes and practices regarding Ashta vibhrama assessment among Ayurvedic practitioners: A cross-sectional study to inform development of a standardized assessment tool.
journal: Journal of Ayurveda and integrative medicine
abstract: Ashta vibhrama comprising eight domains of mental and behavioural disturbances described in Ayurveda Psychiatry forms an important component of the clinical assessment of unmada. However, its clinical assessment remains largely practitioner dependent with limited standardization and variability in interpretation and application. To assess the knowledge, attitude, and practice (KAP) of Ayurvedic practitioners regarding the Ashta Vibhrama assessment, identify areas requiring improvements and examining their association with years of clinical experience. A cross-sectional, questionnaire-based exploratory needs assessment study was conducted among Ayurveda practitioners involved in teaching and/or practice of Manasa Roga. An 18-item researcher developed questionnaire, comprising 16 closed ended and 2 open ended questions was administered online through REDCap and distributed via e-mail and whatsapp. The questionnaire was informed by the classical Ashta vibhrama framework and the KAP approach and underwent expert review for relevance of content and clarity. However, it was not formally retested. Quantitative data were analysed using descriptive statistics, while open ended responses were analysed thematically. Sixty-three practitioners participated in the survey among them 47 were faculty members and 16 were independently practicing clinicians. Most respondents demonstrated familiarity with the conceptual framework of Ashta vibhrama. Approximately 81% perceived variability in its assessment. 84% indicated a need for greater standardization and 93.7% endorsed the need for a standardized assessment tool. Qualitative responses highlighted the need for standardized assessment protocols, operational definitions, structured scoring, clinical guidance and training with barriers including inter-practitioner variability, difficulty in assessing mental and behavioural changes. The findings provide preliminary need assessment evidence supporting the development and psychometric validation of a standardized Ashta vibhrama assessment instrument. These findings should be interpreted as exploratory because the KAP questionnaire was not formally pretested or psychometrically validated.

title: Uncovering the genetic architecture of optic nerve integrity estimates through genome-wide association study meta-analyses.
authors: van der Heide Frank C T
van der Kallen Carla J H
abstract: The peripapillary retinal nerve fibre layer (pRNFL) thickness and Bruch's membrane opening-minimum rim width (BMO-MRW) are structural biomarkers for glaucoma. We conducted large-scale multi-cohort genome-wide association meta-analyses of global and sectoral pRNFL thickness and BMO-MRW to disentangle their genetic architecture. We included up to 25,942 and 12,080 participants for global and sectoral pRNFL thickness and BMO-MRW, respectively, from the International Glaucoma Genetics Consortium. Conditional analysis was used to identify loci with association evidence beyond intraocular pressure (IOP). Genes at these loci were prioritised to identify candidate causal genes using transcriptome-wide association studies and colocalisation of genetic and expression quantitative trait loci. Nine loci were identified for each of global pRNFL thickness and global BMO-MRW. The analyses further revealed 20 and 11 loci for pRNFL and BMO-MRW sectors, respectively, comprising both shared and sector-specific loci. Interestingly, the effect sizes of rs1313237, a well-known optic nerve locus, had opposite effect directions between pRNFL temporal and nasal regions. Robust associations were observed for genes relevant to IOP-adjusted glaucoma biology, including NMNAT2 and TRIOBP. Our findings highlighted the potential neurodegenerative or developmental genes identified for pRNFL thickness and BMO-MRW whose effects are not fully mediated by IOP. We also elucidated genetic differences among pRNFL sectors, which require further investigation to assess clinical relevance. P.G. is supported by an Investigator Grant and an Ideas Grant from the Australian National Health and Medical Research Council (NHMRC), and D.A.M. is supported by a Stan Perron Charitable Foundation People's Grant.

title: The role of intensive-care-unit fluid balance in patients with aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage: A single-center retrospective study.
abstract: While liberal fluid use is common to prevent vasospasm-related hypoperfusion in aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage (aSAH), excess fluids can cause cerebral edema, impair microcirculation, and worsen outcomes. This study explores the role of fluid balancing in the ICU and its potential as a predictor of aSAH outcomes. The cumulative intensive care unit (ICU) fluid balance was evaluated in all consecutive aneurysmal aSAH cases treated between 01/2003 and 08/2024 (n = 1318). Primary endpoints included delayed cerebral ischemia (DCI)-related infarction, in-hospital mortality, and unfavorable 6-month outcomes (modified Rankin Scale >3). Multivariable models were adjusted for treated vasospasm and baseline characteristics; sensitivity analyses addressed ICU length of stay, treatment era, early death and residual confounding. Cumulative ICU fluid balance ranged from -12.5 L to + 80.5 L. Each 5-L increase was associated with DCI-related infarction (aOR:1.47, 95%-CI:1.30-1.67) and unfavorable 6-month outcome (aOR:1.82, 95%-CI:1.58-2.11); the latter remained robust after adjustment for ICU-length-of-stay (aOR:1.97, 95%-CI:1.70-2.31). In-hospital mortality was associated with mean daily fluid balance (aOR:3.19 per L/day, 95%-CI:2.44-4.23) and with cumulative balance only after accounting for ICU stay. A data-derived cut-off of + 3.8 L corresponded to the cohort median and was unstable. Higher cumulative ICU fluid balance was dose-dependently associated with complications and, most robustly, with poor functional outcome after aSAH. Because fluid balance partly reflects treatment and complication duration, it should be regarded as a marker of a complicated course that may also contribute to harm. Prospective studies are needed to clarify causality.

title: Telerehabilitation and teleassessment in rare pediatric neurological disorders: an ERN-RND telerehabilitation working group systematic review.
abstract: Children and adolescents with rare neurological disorders (RNDs) often require long-term rehabilitation, but specialist access is limited by geography, medical fragility, and travel burden. Telerehabilitation and teleassessment may extend care into the home, yet evidence remains fragmented. We evaluated functional outcomes and summarized feasibility, adherence, acceptability, safety, and teleassessment measurement properties. This PROSPERO-registered systematic review (CRD420251238931) followed PRISMA and SWiM guidance. PubMed, Scopus, IEEE Xplore, and Google Scholar were searched through April 20, 2026, supplemented by citation searching. Eligible studies evaluated telerehabilitation or teleassessment in participants aged ≤18 years with Orphanet-classified RNDs and reported child-level functional outcomes. Mixed cohorts required separable data or ≥80% eligible participants. Two reviewers independently screened records, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias and certainty of evidence using design-appropriate tools. 2,260 unique records were screened and 71 full texts assessed; 16 studies were included. 13 evaluated telerehabilitation (316 participants: 203 intervention, 113 comparator/control) and 3 evaluated teleassessment (94 participants). Most studies involved neuromuscular disorders, mainly Duchenne or Becker muscular dystrophy; other conditions included Rett syndrome, Fragile X syndrome, Dravet syndrome, Canavan disease, Guillain-Barré syndrome, and rare pediatric ataxias. Technologies included videoconferencing, apps, wearable sensors, and video-based assessment. Telerehabilitation was associated with improvement or stabilization in selected motor, respiratory, cognitive, communication, and daily functional outcomes, whereas global measures often showed limited short-term change. Feasibility, adherence, and acceptability were generally favorable. No major telerehabilitation-related safety concerns were reported when assessed. Teleassessment showed good reliability or agreement with in-person motor assessment. In selected pediatric RNDs, telerehabilitation and teleassessment demonstrate strong feasibility, high acceptability, and meaningful clinical potential as effective complements to in-person care. These approaches offer valuable opportunities to expand access, enhance continuity of care, and support patient-centered rehabilitation. Larger multicenter studies should evaluate long-term outcomes and equitable implementation.

title: Moral injury in researchers and what to do about it.
Medical Reasoning in Large Language Models: Development and Evaluation of the MedEvalArena Benchmark.
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) perform strongly on medical specialty board multiple-choice questions (MCQs) but underperform in complex medical reasoning. This gap indicates a need to improve LLM medical reasoning and evaluation paradigms. This study aimed to develop and evaluate MedEvalArena, a dynamically regenerable benchmark for assessing medical reasoning in LLMs. In a symmetric round-robin format, 6 frontier LLMs from the OpenAI, Grok, Gemini, Claude, Kimi, and DeepSeek families generated challenging board-style medical MCQs, adjudicated question validity on an ensemble LLM-as-judge panel, and answered the validated examination. Candidate items were generated until each model contributed 50 validated questions according to Association of American Medical Colleges (AAMC)/American Board of Medical Specialties (ABMS) physician specialty distributions, yielding a 300-question examination. Judges adjudicated candidate questions' logical validity and medical accuracy. We compared question-generation validity rates, assessed leave-one-out judge agreement, and tested for self-judging preference. Questions were audited for overlap with public MedQA (medical question-answering) benchmarks. We tested question-answering (QA) accuracy across LLMs using a binomial-logit generalized linear mixed model likelihood-ratio test. A generator-stratified 90-question subset was completed by 5 board-certified physicians for paired human-LLM analysis. We evaluated inference cost-accuracy tradeoffs. Multiple comparisons were adjusted by the Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) procedure. Judge-panel validity rates were significantly higher for questions generated by OpenAI (94.8%, Wilson 95% CI 85.9%-98.2%), Gemini (92.3%, 95% CI 83.2%-96.7%), and Claude (83.3%, 95% CI 72.6%-90.4%) models than those generated by Kimi (63.8%, 95% CI 54.3%-72.4%), Grok (56%, 95% CI 45.8%-65.8%), and DeepSeek (46.0%, 95% CI 37.4%-54.7%). Kimi also demonstrated significantly higher validity than DeepSeek (2-sample tests of proportions; BH-adjusted P=.01). The public-source similarity audit found no exact or near-duplicate matches. Leave-one-out judge agreement was moderate. Generator-specific same-family judging coefficients were nonnegative (0 to 11.0 percentage points); however, none remained significant after BH adjustment. There was no significant difference between the 6 frontier LLM QA accuracies, which ranged from 85.7% (257/300) to 91.7% (275/300), on the 300-question examination (generalized linear mixed model likelihood-ratio test P=.07). The study had 80% power to detect LLM accuracy differences of 9.2 percentage points; nonsignificance did not establish equivalence. On the 90-question subset, physician accuracy was 85.6% (95% CI 79.4%-91.7%; stratified normal with finite-population correction), compared with aggregate LLM performance of 94.4% (85/90; Wilson 95% CI 87.6%-97.6%). This difference was not significant (McNemar test, P=.08); however, the study was powered to detect a human vs LLM accuracy difference of 14% to 15%. Answering-only costs varied by nearly 2 orders of magnitude, with multiple models on the cost-accuracy Pareto frontier. MedEvalArena enables scalable, regenerable, peer-judged benchmarking of LLM medical reasoning. Question-generation validity differentiated model families more clearly than answering accuracy, suggesting that valid MCQ generation may complement QA benchmarks for assessing LLM medical reasoning.
